historical_references.reference: Gildardo, son of Alaric I, was a Visigothic king who ruled from 522 to 531 AD. He succeeded his father and is known for his efforts to establish a stable and just rule, as well as his patronage of the arts and learning.

Gildardo, a bishop of Toledo during the Reconquista period (632-1037 AD), is known for his role in the Cristianización de España (Christianization of Spain). He played a significant part in converting the last Moorish kingdom, Granada, to Christianity and was instrumental in the creation of the Church of the Holy Savior in Toledo.
